title: SLO Snapshot and Capacity Freeze Procedure
author: Miguel Ramos
summary: Procedure for taking authoritative SLO snapshots and performing a controlled capacity freeze to stabilize error budgets during major incidents, maintenance windows, or policy-driven gating.
content:
Overview:

This document defines the SLO Snapshot and Capacity Freeze Procedure — a lightweight, auditable process used by SRE to preserve SLO state and limit capacity changes that could accelerate error-budget consumption. The goal is to create a reproducible snapshot of SLO telemetry and service capacity allocations, apply a minimal set of protective controls (the "freeze"), and provide clear unfreeze and rollback steps. Use this procedure for: major incident containment, cross-region maintenance, contractual freeze windows, and pre-rollout safety during high-risk experiments.

When to run the procedure:
- Emergency incident where error budget burn rate > 5x normal for 15+ minutes and containment actions risk further instability.
- Planned system-wide maintenance expected to shift traffic or capacity allocations across tenants.
- Contractual/customer freeze windows requested by Enterprise with >72hr notice (follow legal/compliance checklist).
- High-risk model or runtime rollout flagged by Product/Research with a canary rollback requirement.

Owners and roles:
- Procedure Owner: SRE Capacity Guild (primary on-call: capacity-lead@redwood.com)
- Incident Lead: assigned during incident (must be an SRE lead)
- Telemetry Custodian: Observability team (owns snapshot exports)
- Change Executor: Infra Automation team (applies freeze controls)
- Notifier: Incident Commander (communicates status to stakeholders)

Preflight checklist (run before any freeze):
1. Confirm decision authority (Incident Lead + Capacity Guild approval).
2. Record affected services and SLOs (service name, SLO id, target, rolling window).
3. Ensure runbook and channel opened: #incident-<id> and incident doc created.
4. Notify Legal/Account teams if customer-impacting or contractual.
5. Verify access to automation tools (kubectl/terraform/infractl) and snapshot storage (s3://sre-snapshots/).

Step A — SLO snapshot (authoritative telemetry export):
1. Identify SLOs to snapshot. Minimum data set: 30d rolling target, 7d rolling observed, 1h burn-rate series, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and per-tenant token consumption.
2. Run the snapshot export command (Observability CLI):
   ```bash
   obsctl export-slo --service <service> --slo-ids <id1,id2> --window 30d --out /tmp/slo-<service>-snapshot-$(date +%F-%H%M).json
   obsctl export-metrics --service <service> --metrics latency,p99,error_rate,token_consumption --window 7d --downsample 1m --out /tmp/metrics-<service>-7d-$(date +%F).ndjson
   ```
3. Verify checksum and upload to snapshot bucket:
   ```bash
   sha256sum /tmp/slo-*.json | tee /tmp/checksums.txt
   aws s3 cp /tmp/slo-*.json s3://sre-snapshots/<incident-id>/ --acl internal-read
   aws s3 cp /tmp/metrics-*.ndjson s3://sre-snapshots/<incident-id>/
   ```
4. Add snapshot artifact entries to the incident doc (link the S3 paths) and tag with the incident id.

Table: Snapshot artifacts (example format)
| artifact | path | owner | retention | notes |
| SLO snapshot JSON | s3://sre-snapshots/INC-2026-045/slo-service-a-2026-06-12.json | Observability | 90d | includes per-tenant slices |
| Metric ndjson | s3://sre-snapshots/INC-2026-045/metrics-service-a-7d.ndjson | Observability | 30d | 1m downsampled |

Step B — Freeze intent and levels:
- Freeze Level 0 (Informational): request-only; no automated changes. Use when burn rate < 3x and risk low.
- Freeze Level 1 (Protective): block non-essential capacity changes (no new cluster pools, no autoscaler policy increases). Allowed: emergency scaling down and controlled failovers.
- Freeze Level 2 (Strict): suspend all automated scale-ups, prevent tenant move/eviction, force minimal new work (reject best-effort and backlog jobs). Use when burn rate > 5x.
- Freeze Level 3 (Quarantine): strict isolation for affected services; redirect traffic to safe fallbacks. Trigger only with Exec approval.

Freeze decision matrix (decision thresholds):
| Condition | Suggested level | Decision authority |
| Burn rate 3x–5x sustained 15m | Level 1 | Incident Lead + Capacity Guild |
| Burn rate >5x 15m or multi-region errors | Level 2 | Incident Lead + VP SRE |
| Data plane compromise or cascading failures | Level 3 | CTO or Exec on-duty |

Step C — Applying a freeze (automation steps):
1. Record freeze in incident doc: freeze-level, rationale, start_time, requested_by.
2. Run the dry-run to see impacted changes:
   ```bash
   infractl freeze --service <service> --level <0|1|2|3> --dry-run --out /tmp/freeze-preview.json
   ```
3. Review preview with Capacity Guild (5–15 min).
4. Commit freeze:
   ```bash
   infractl freeze --service <service> --level 2 --commit --incident INC-2026-045 --reason "High burn rate"
   ```
   The command records the freeze in the central ledger and updates the capacity-controller to enforce policies.
5. Verify enforcement: check policy endpoints and autoscaler logs:
   ```bash
   curl -s https://capacity-controller.internal/services/<service>/policy | jq .enforced_freeze
   kubectl get hpa -n <ns> | grep <service>
   ```
6. Communicate freeze to stakeholders and downstream teams (use incident channel template).

Monitoring and verification during freeze:
- Telemetry Custodian runs 5m validation queries to ensure no unintended scale-ups. Example query:
  - "SELECT sum(scale_ops) FROM autoscaler WHERE time > now() - 5m AND service = '<service>'"
- Use synthetic canaries (if available) to validate that critical paths respond at acceptable p95 latency.
- Log any failed automation attempts and surface to change executor.

Unfreeze and rollback procedure:
1. Preconditions to unfreeze:
   - Burn rate reduced to <2x baseline for at least 30 minutes OR
   - Incident has a confirmed mitigation that removes root cause risk.
2. Prepare staged unfreeze plan (Level-by-Level):
   a. Level 2 -> Level 1 (validate for 30 minutes)
   b. Level 1 -> Level 0 (validate for 30 minutes)
   c. Level 0 -> lifted (final confirmation)
3. Execute unfreeze with infractl in staged mode:
   ```bash
   infractl freeze --service <service> --level 1 --commit --incident INC-2026-045 --note "staged unfreeze: 2->1"
   sleep 1800
   infractl freeze --service <service> --level 0 --commit --incident INC-2026-045 --note "staged unfreeze: 1->0"
   ```
4. Post-unfreeze validation: run traffic and SLO smoke tests, confirm per-tenant token accounting, and ensure no immediate re-escalation.
5. Close freeze in incident doc and add links to artifacts.

Rollback (if unfreeze causes regression):
- Re-apply previous freeze level with infractl and annotate the incident doc with the new decision path. Capture the reason and timeline.

Audit and evidence collection (post-incident):
- Export the freeze ledger for the incident:
  ```bash
  infractl freeze-ledger export --incident INC-2026-045 --out s3://sre-snapshots/INC-2026-045/freeze-ledger.json
  ```
- Include snapshot artifacts, freeze ledger, and command checksums in the post-incident review packet.
- Recommended retention: freeze ledger 3 years, SLO snapshots 90 days (extend for contractual incidents).

Edge cases and guidance:
- Multi-tenant shared GPU pools: prioritize tenant-affecting freezes conservatively; prefer tenant-scoped throttles over global freezes.
- Customer-requested freeze: require signed request + legal approval. Follow the Customer Freeze Appendix (link in related pages).
- Emergency infra changes: if freezing blocks necessary emergency remediation (e.g., kernel patch that requires autoscaler changes), incident lead may temporarily relax controls — document and re-snapshot before and after.

Metrics to capture for continuous improvement:
- Time-to-snapshot (target <7 minutes from decision).
- Time-to-enforce-freeze (target <10 minutes from commit).
- False-positive freeze rate (freezes that did not change burn trajectory).
- Unfreeze rollback frequency and root causes.

Appendices:
A. Incident channel freeze template (paste into #incident-<id>):
- Freeze Level: <0|1|2|3>
- Rationale: <short description>
- Affected services: <svc-a, svc-b>
- Snapshot artifacts: <links>
- Start time: <UTC timestamp>
- Expected review cadence: every 30m

B. Minimal CLI toolset (versions):
- obsctl v1.4.2+
- infractl v2.0.0-beta3
- awscli v2.11.0

C. Contacts and escalation points:
- Capacity Guild Slack: #capacity-guild (primary)
- Observability on-call: observability-rotations@redwood.com
- Infra Automation on-call: infra-ops@redwood.com

D. Related policies and pages:
- Service onboarding and SLO admission playbook: /confluence/eng-sre/capacity-planning/service-onboarding-runway-and-slo-admission-playbook-2026.json
- SLO rollback confidence scoring: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/slo-rollback-confidence-scoring-playbook-2027.json

Document maintenance:
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any freeze > Level 2.
- Owner for updates: Capacity Guild lead (update the date and reviewers on change).

Questions or suggestions: open a PR against this page or reach out to Miguel Ramos (miguel.ramos@redwood.com).
